definition: Streamlit turns Python scripts into interactive web apps — ideal for data dashboards and AI demos.
details: Created by Adrien Treuille, Thiago Teixeira and Amanda Kelly in 2019; acquired by Snowflake in 2022.

explainer.lead: How to install Streamlit, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.
explainer.createdBy: Adrien Treuille, Thiago Teixeira, Amanda Kelly; Snowflake.
explainer.inAi: Build a chat UI or model playground in pure Python in minutes.
explainer.jsNote: Streamlit is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.

tiers.eli5: Like turning a recipe you wrote on paper into a working kitchen display without building the kitchen yourself.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers wrap model or data code in a Streamlit script to get a shareable interactive app fast. Pitfall: it is built for demos and dashboards, so production-scale apps with complex state can outgrow it.
tiers.paperLevel: A tool that converts Python scripts into interactive web apps. Created by Adrien Treuille, Thiago Teixeira and Amanda Kelly in 2019; acquired by Snowflake in 2022.

explainer.example: A data scientist writes a short Python script that loads a model and a text box, and Streamlit serves it as a web page where visitors type input and see predictions.
